reason: Household batteries contain toxic electrolytes and heavy metals. Cutting heating or dismantling batteries causes chemical burns or explosion.
Never attempt DIY repair on degraded swollen or leaking battery cells.
Spent batteries must not be repurposed for craft or hobby projects.
Tape positive terminals with electrical tape and use dedicated e-waste battery collection bin.
Melting or burning plastic at home releases carcinogenic dioxins and hazardous fumes.
Use utility knives with care and keep cutting strokes away from hands.
Clean plastic containers are safe for non-toxic dry storage and gardening.
Cutting and binding plastic items with tape or non-toxic adhesives is safe.
Rinsing and flattening plastic containers presents no significant safety hazard.
Cutting or scoring glass requires safety glasses and protective cut-resistant gloves.
source: OSHA Hand and Eye Safety Standards

reason: Washing and reusing intact glass bottles and jars is safe for household use.
Decorating or filling glass jars with soil/pebbles without scoring is safe.
Sorting and rinsing unbroken glass containers is safe.
Cutting or punching metal tins creates sharp jagged edges. Use safety gloves.
Using smooth-rimmed clean tins for storage is safe.
Punching drainage holes with a hammer and nail is safe when wearing eye protection.
Compressing clean cans and foil is safe.
Paper handling cutting and binding is inherently safe for all household users.
Always use a cutting mat and keep fingers behind the blade path when using utility knives.
Reusing clean cartons for storage and mailing is safe.
Cutting and gluing cardboard organizers is safe.
Flattening and tying cardboard bundles is safe.
Take care with sharp needles and pins during sewing and mending.
Cutting clean worn garments into dusting cloths is safe.
Transforming fabric into bags with standard scissors and thread is safe.
Folding clean clothes for donation or textile drop-off is safe.
Use shoe adhesives in a well-ventilated room or outdoors away from open flames.
Using clean worn footwear for yard work is safe.
Tying shoe pairs for donation or recycling bin drop-off is safe.
Layering vegetable peels and leaves in a compost pit is safe. Wash hands after handling.
Segregating kitchen food scraps into green bins is safe.
Bagging non-recyclable refuse for municipal collection is safe.
Do not perform acid leaching solvent extraction or open burning on any household waste.
